title: Irländsk köttstuvning (Irish Meat Stew)
description: Prepared with lamb, onions, and white pepper.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water, cut into small pieces and place in the bottom of a pot.
Peel the onion, parboil, cut into slices and place with the seasonings on top of the meat.
Add the boiling water and let the meat cook slowly for ¼ hour.
Then add the peeled and sliced potatoes, and let the stew cook another ½ hour approximately.
Serve the meat in the middle of the platter, potatoes around it, and pour the sauce over.

title: Italiensk soppa (Italian Soup)
description: A soup made with meat, fat, and white pepper.
steps: Brown the meat bones in the fat
Add 4 liters of water and bring to a boil
Skim well when it boils, then add seasonings, carrots, and the parsley bunch
Cook covered with a tight-fitting lid until the broth has good flavor, about 4–5 hours
Strain and skim the broth well
Fry together the butter and flour, add the broth, and add the rinsed star-shaped pasta
Let the broth cook about 20 minutes, or until the pasta is completely soft and swollen
Add the grated cheese and wine, taste and adjust seasoning

title: Jelly with Cooked Sugar (Gelé med kokt socker)
description: Prepared with fruit juice, sugar, and water.
steps: Prepare the juice as previously described.
Chop the sugar into small pieces, place it in a preserving pan, pour the water over it, and let the pan stand beside the stove until the sugar is dissolved.
Place the pan over the fire, and let the mixture cook, skimming it well, until all the water has evaporated and the sugar is dry.
Towards the end of cooking, stir the sugar continuously with a wooden spoon so it does not burn at the bottom of the pan.
Add the juice at once, little by little, otherwise the enamel of the pan will crack.
When the sugar has melted, let the jelly cook about 5 minutes; it is ready when a drop of it, poured on a plate, sets quickly.
Bind the jars when the jelly is set.

title: Jordärtskockor ä la Idun (Jerusalem Artichokes à la Idun)
description: Prepared with jerusalem artichokes, truffles, and jerusalem artichoke.
steps: Prepare and cook the Jerusalem artichokes as in the previous recipe.
Remove with a slotted spoon, let cool and cut into 3 mm thick slices.
Cut the truffle into thin slices and mix with the Jerusalem artichokes.
Place them in 6 small shells buttered with half of the butter.
Pour white sauce over; sprinkle the arrangement with grated cheese and crushed rusks, melt the remaining butter and pour over.
Place the shells in a baking pan with coarse salt and gratinize in a warm oven 10-15 minutes.
Serve immediately on a round platter with a folded napkin, garnished with parsley or salad.

title: Jordärtskockspuré (Jerusalem Artichoke Purée)
description: Prepared with jerusalem artichokes, celery, and stock.
steps: Wash and scrape the Jerusalem artichokes (preferably under running water), wash again, and let them soak for 1 hour in 1 1/2 liters water mixed with {{source-12}} and {{source-13}} to prevent darkening.

title: Judebröd (Jewish Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with egg white, wheat flour, and bitter almonds.
steps: Wash the butter and stir it with the sugar for 15 minutes.
Work in the egg, egg white, the grated almond, the finely crushed cardamom and lastly the flour, which should be sifted and well mixed with the hartshorn salt.
Roll out the dough to approximately 2 mm thickness and cut with a round measure into small cakes.
Brush the cakes with egg white, sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon and bake golden brown in a not too warm oven.

title: Jägarbiff (Hunter's Beef Patties)
description: Prepared with veal, rusks, and cream.
steps: Prepare the meat, cut into pieces and grind 4 times through a meat grinder.
Mix the crushed rusks with the cream and let swell for 1 hour.
Work the meat well with the rusk mixture, season with the spices and form into 15 round patties.
Brown the patties quickly in butter and place in a pot.
Cut the mushrooms into slices and sauté in butter in the frying pan, add flour and mix well with the butter and mushrooms.
Add the meat stock and cream and bring the sauce to a good boil, season with spices.
Pour the sauce over the patties, which then cook slowly with a tightly closed lid for 10-15 minutes.
Place on a warm serving dish, whisk up the sauce and pour over the patties.
Serve with mashed potatoes or fried potatoes.

title: Järpe i Gelé (Grouse in Aspic)
description: Prepared with grouse, broth or water, and marrow.

ingredients.name: mayonnaise sauce, poached eggs, cooked beets or oysters
ingredients.sourceText: mayonnaise sauce, poached eggs, cooked beets or oysters

steps: Roast the grouse whole and let them cool.
Cook broth from the ox meat and calf's foot, which when done should make 1½ liters.
Strain the broth, skim it well, and return it to the heat.

Add the gelatin dissolved in a little water, and when the broth is warm, whisk in the eggs, and bring the broth to a good boil while stirring, then strain through a napkin or cheesecloth wrung out in hot water.
Pour half of the clear aspic onto a flat plate to set.
From the cooled roasted grouse, cut 4–5 slices on each side of the breastbone.
Place these slices on the set aspic, pour the remaining aspic over, and set everything out to set.
Separate the meat slices with a knife from the rest.

title: Järpe i Gelé (Partridge in Aspic)
description: Prepared with partridges, broth, and meat.
steps: Clean the partridges, singe them, remove the innards and cut off wings and bones.
Rinse them very well, dry with a meat cloth and truss (see poultry).
Brown the butter in a roasting pan, place the partridges in breast-side up and roast in a warm oven for about 1/2 hour, basting frequently and adding broth.
Remove and let cool, then carefully loosen the breasts from the carcasses; cut each breast half into 3 slices.
Place the carcasses back in the roasting pan, add more broth and let it cook with the meat bones until reduced to about 1/2 liter.
Strain the broth, let cool and carefully skim off all fat.
Prepare the aspic as in recipe no. 181; when cold, add the wine.
Pour a little of the clear aspic into the bottom of 12 rinsed partridge molds and place on ice to set.
Decorate the molds with truffle cut into attractive shapes.
Pour a few drops of aspic over the garnish and let set so the garnish doesn't move when the meat is added.
Place half a partridge breast in each mold so it appears whole with the outer side against the garnish, then fill the molds with aspic.
Place the molds in a cold place to set.
Pour the remaining aspic onto a platter and let set.
Cut a cone-shaped croûton from day-old wheat bread, hollow out the top, wrap with foil and place in the center of a large round silver or porcelain platter.
Place flowers and greens in the top of the croûton.
Turn the partridge breasts out of the molds and stand them against the croûton.
Decorate between them with piped aspic and around the platter with small triangular aspic croûtons decorated with chopped truffle.
Garnish the arrangement with the inner light lettuce leaves and serve as an entrée with mayonnaise.

title: Jäsmunkar (Yeast Puffs)
description: Prepared with yeast, sour milk, and melted butter.

ingredients.name: 1 kkp applesauce or red currant jelly
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kkp applesauce or red currant jelly

steps: The milk, which should be lukewarm, is mixed with the butter, the beaten eggs, the sugar, and the blanched and grated almonds.
Add the flour and the yeast stirred in 1 tsk. sugar, and work the dough until it becomes smooth and glossy, then let it stand in a warm place to rise for approximately 2 hours.
Work the dough on the baking board, roll it out to 1 cm. thickness, and cut it with a round measure into cakes about 6 cm. in diameter.
Place a little applesauce or red currant jelly in the middle of each cake; brush the edges with egg white and press them together well.
Place the puffs on a floured baking sheet and let them rise for approximately 1 1/2 hours.
Cook them in moderately hot lard until they are cooked through and a beautiful brown, place them on absorbent paper and let them drain.
Sprinkle with sugar and serve warm with coffee or tea.

Add the flour and the yeast dissolved in 1 tsp. sugar, and work the dough until it becomes smooth and shiny, then let it rise in a warm place for approx. 2 hours.
Work the dough on the baking board, roll it out to 1 cm. thickness and cut it out with a round cutter into cakes, which should be approx. 6 cm. in diameter.
Place a little applesauce or red currant jelly on the middle of each cake; brush the edges with egg white and press them well together.
Place the puffs on a floured baking sheet and let them rise for approx. 1 1/2 hours.
Cook them in moderately hot lard until they are thoroughly cooked and a beautiful brown, place them on absorbent paper and let them drain.
Dust with sugar and serve warm with coffee or tea.

title: Jäst Hallonsaft (Fermented Raspberry Juice)
description: Prepared with raspberries, vinegar, and water.

ingredients.name: sugar per kilogram of juice
ingredients.sourceText: 0.25 kg sugar per kilogram of juice

steps: Crush the berries and place them in a crock. Pour the warm water and vinegar over them, and let the berries ferment for about 8 days, or until they float up. Stir the berries once a day.
Pour them into cheesecloth to drain. Place the juice with the sugar and let it cook until it is clear and glossy.
Bottle it hot or cold; cork the bottles and seal with resin.

description: A pudding made with cod or fish, rice, and butter or cream.

ingredients.name: okokt kabiljo or 1/2 lit. kokt, hackad fisk (uncooked cod or cooked, chopped fish)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 kg. okokt kabiljo or 1/2 lit. kokt, hackad fisk (uncooked cod or cooked, chopped fish)

ingredients.name: 3 msk. smör or flottyr (butter or cream)

steps: Fisken vattenlägges dagen innan den skall användas (the fish is soaked in water the day before it is to be used)
Den kokas, får kallna, alla ben tagas bort och kabeljon hackas fint (it is cooked, allowed to cool, all bones are removed and the cod is chopped finely)
Grynen sköljas, sättas på elden i kallt vatten (the groats are rinsed, placed on the stove in cold water)
När detta kokar, tillsättes mjölken (when this boils, the milk is added)
Grynen få nästan färdigkoka, smöret eller flottyren sättes till (the groats are allowed to almost finish cooking, the butter or cream is added)
Gröten slås upp att kallna (the porridge is beaten and allowed to cool)
En form smörjes och beströs med stötta skorpor (a mold is buttered and sprinkled with breadcrumbs)
I de kalla grynen nedröras kryddorna, den hackade fisken och de uppvispade äggen (the seasonings, the chopped fish and the beaten eggs are stirred into the cold groats)
Massan hälles därpå i formen, beströs med stötta skorpor och krusas nätt (the mixture is poured into the mold, sprinkled with breadcrumbs and decorated neatly)
Puddingen sättes i god ugnsvärme att grädda under 1 tim. (the pudding is placed in a hot oven to bake for 1 hour)
Serveras med skirat smör (served with clarified butter)

title: Kalkon, färserad med kastanjer (Turkey Stuffed with Chestnuts)
description: Prepared with turkey, chestnuts, and white pepper.
steps: Treat the turkey as in no. 605 and rub with a mixture of salt and pepper.
Peel the chestnuts and let them lie in hot water until the inner thin skin can be removed with a cloth.
Place the peeled chestnuts in the broth together with the butter and seasonings and cook until tender but do not let them fall apart.
Drain in a colander and let cool.
Fill the turkey with the chestnuts, treat thereafter as in the preceding recipe and roast either in the oven or in a pot.
Carve it, garnish with small sausages, browned potatoes and green salad.
Serve with gravy or prepared sauce (see no. 429).

title: Kall ananaspudding (Cold Pineapple Pudding)
description: A pudding made with pineapple, cream, and egg yolks.
steps: Bring 3 parts of the cream, the egg yolks, and the sugar to a boil over heat with whisking until the cream thickens.
Continue whisking until the cream becomes cold.
Beat the remaining cream to stiff peaks and stir in together with pineapple, cut into small pieces, and the sherry.
Last stir in the gelatin sheets dissolved in pineapple juice.
Pour the cream into a water-rinsed and sugared mold and set it out to stiffen.
Dip the mold briefly in lukewarm water, turn out the pudding and garnish with pineapple.

title: Kall ananaspudding (Cold Pineapple Pudding)
description: A pudding made with pineapple, egg yolks, and egg white.
steps: Cut one quarter of the pineapple into small cubes, from which all juice is pressed out into a linen cloth.

Whip the egg yolks, egg white, sugar, wine and half of the pineapple juice in a saucepan over the fire until the mixture is thick and foamy, then remove the saucepan and continue whisking until the cream is cold.
Rinse the gelatin with cold water and dissolve it in the rest of the pineapple juice, which has been heated beforehand.
Whip the cream until stiff peaks form.
First blend the pineapple pieces into the cream, then the gelatin, and last fold in the cream very carefully.
Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-dusted mold and let it sit on ice for 3-4 hours.

When the pudding is to be served, loosen it from the edge with a pointed knife and turn it out onto a flat glass plate lined with parchment paper. Garnish with the rest of the pineapple, sliced thinly. One pineapple is enough for 12 people, as the slices with which the pudding is garnished can be divided.

title: Kall hummersås (Cold Lobster Sauce)
description: A sauce made with roe, vinegar, and salad oil.

Add the vinegar and salad oil, little by little, while stirring.

title: Kall rispudding (Cold Rice Pudding Riz à l'Impératrice for 6-8 Persons)

Turn out, garnish with red currant jelly and serve with apricot sauce or strawberry juice.

title: Kall Rispudding (Cold Rice Pudding)
description: A pudding made with rice, vanilla pod or lemon, and gelatin.

ingredients.name: 1/2 vanilla pod or the grated zest of 1/4 lemon
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 vanilla pod or the grated zest of 1/4 lemon

steps: Rinse the rice grains, scald them in hot water, add them to the boiling milk and let them cook with the vanilla or lemon zest, stirring, until they are completely soft.
Thin with more milk if needed.
The porridge, which should be thick, is poured out and allowed to cool, after which the sugar is added.

Fill the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-sprinkled timbale mold and let it set on ice for 3-4 hours.
Turn out, garnish with currant jelly and serve with apricot sauce or strawberry juice.

The rice can be mixed with cherries, peaches or other fruits, cut into cubes. On the bottom of the mold, 1 dcl. wine jelly, colored red with carmine, can be poured, allowed to set, after which the rice mixture is added and allowed to set on ice.

The rice mixture can be filled into a ring mold, set on ice, turned out onto a round dish, preferably of silver, the hole in the middle filled with compote of strawberries, raspberries or apricots, and the rice border garnished with berries or fruit.

title: Kall äppelpudding (Cold Apple Pudding)
description: A pudding made with white wine, apples, and lemon.
steps: Make a clear, simmering liquid by boiling the sugar, wine and water together.
Wash, dry and peel the apples, cut them into wedges, remove the cores and place directly in the sugar liquid.
Add the lemon peel and cook the apples until they become a puree.
Pass the apple puree through a hair sieve and flavor with lemon juice and more sugar if desired.
Rinse the gelatin in cold water, cut it into pieces, dissolve it in hot water and mix well with the apple puree.
Immediately fill the mixture into a water-rinsed and sugar-sprinkled à-la-daube mold of porcelain and let stand on ice for approximately 5 hours.
When the pudding is to be served, carefully loosen it around the edge with a pointed knife and turn it out onto a tart plate.
Garnish with biscuits and serve with vanilla sauce or whipped cream. It is best to cook the apple puree the day before the pudding is to be made.

title: Kalops (Beef Stew)
description: Prepared with beef or marrow, white pepper, and onion.

ingredients.name: boneless beef (thigh, rib or marrow bone)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kg boneless beef (thigh, rib or marrow bone)

steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water. It is then cut across the grain into approximately 1½ cm thick slices. The slices are freed from coarser sinews and fat and beaten lightly.
White pepper, salt and flour are mixed on a plate, and in this the meat slices are turned.
The onion is peeled and cut into slices.
The meat and onion are browned quickly in the butter. The browned meat is placed in a pot, the frying pan is whisked out with a little boiling water, which is poured over the meat.
The allspice berries, bay leaves and the remaining water are added, and the kalops is allowed to simmer slowly with a tightly closing lid until the meat feels tender.
It is placed in a serving dish, and the sauce is skimmed.

title: Kalvbiff med stekta ägg (Veal Patties with Fried Eggs)
description: Prepared with veal, eggs, and lard.
steps: Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, cut into pieces and pass together with the lard 4 times through the meat grinder.
Mix the mixture with the beaten eggs and spices and form into round patties, which are brushed with the egg white, whisked with water, and turned in crushed breadcrumbs.
Heat a frying pan slowly, brown the butter in it, place the patties in and fry 2 minutes on each side, after which they are placed on a warm serving platter.
Pour the broth into the pan, which is whisked well, add the tomato puree, let the sauce come to a boil, taste it with the cold butter and the spices and pour over the patties.
Fry the eggs in a griddle and place one egg on each patty.
Serve as a breakfast dish.

title: Kalvbrässkroketter (Calf Thymus Croquettes)
description: Prepared with ox tongue, mushrooms, and broth.
steps: Let the calf thymus soak in water for a couple of hours to remove the blood, then blanch it and let it drain.
Brown it in butter, remove it and let it cool, then cut it into small cubes.
Cut the tongue and mushrooms likewise into cubes.
Fry butter and flour together, add the broth and cream, and let the mixture cook for 5 minutes.
Remove the pan from heat, add the seasonings and egg yolks.
Add the thymus, tongue and mushrooms, and spread the mixture on a flat plate to cool.
Form oblong croquettes, roll them in crushed rusks, dip them in egg and roll them again in crushed rusks, then let them dry for 1/2 hour.
Heat the lard, cook the croquettes until golden brown and arrange on brown paper to drain.
Garnish with parsley and serve with mushroom or tomato sauce.

title: Kalvbrässkroketter (Veal Sweetbread Croquettes)
description: Prepared with veal, sweetbread, and mushrooms.
steps: The veal sweetbread should soak in water for 1 hour to draw out the blood.
Blanch it, place in boiling water with salt added, and let cook 15 minutes, then drain on a sieve; save the stock.
Cut the sweetbread and mushrooms into cubes and sauté in half the butter until the butter is clear, then remove.
Sauté the remaining butter with flour for 2 minutes, add the sweetbread stock, mushroom stock and cream, and let the sauce cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the sweetbread and mushrooms along with the beaten egg yolks and the rinsed gelatin dissolved in 1 msk. hot water.
Season the mixture with spices and place on a flat dish well buttered, and brush with butter on the surface so it does not harden.
When the mass is cold, form portions of about 60 gr. with a spoon and place on a floured board.
Roll the croquettes in flour and form them as ovals.
Dip them in the well-beaten eggs mixed with table oil and seasoned with spices.
Then roll them in the finely crushed bread crumbs and let them sit for 1 hour to harden.
Fry them golden brown in hot lard and place on brown paper to drain.
Serve as a course with tomato or mushroom sauce.

title: Kalvdans (Calf Dance)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, milk, and egg.
steps: Whisk together milk, egg, sugar, salt, and almonds well.
Test a portion of the mixture in a pan over gentle heat.
If the test is too thin, dilute the mixture with cream milk; if too thick, whisk in one or two eggs.
Pour the tested mixture into a water-rinsed mold and bake in a water bath in the oven or on the stove.
In the latter case, the mold should be covered.
When the kalvdans is set and has turned a nice brown color, remove and serve with milk or fruit sauce.

steps: Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and cut into 6 slices, which are flattened to half their thickness and rubbed with the spices.

For the egg custard, beat the egg yolks and egg white well with the cream or broth and a little salt. Pour the mixture into a well-buttered mold or bowl with a lid and place in a pot with boiling water. When it has set after about 1/2 hour it is done and is then cut into 6 squares.

Fry the fillets about 3 minutes on each side and place on a warm serving platter. Whisk out the frying pan with the broth and pour the sauce over the meat. Fry the mushrooms in the butter until it is clear, place one egg square on each fillet and the mushrooms around it.
Garnish with parsley and serve very hot with browned potatoes as a breakfast dish.

title: Kalvhjärnakotletter (Calf Brain Cutlets)
description: Prepared with rusks, peas, and water.
steps: Let the brain soak in water, changing frequently to draw out all blood.
Blanch the brain and place on a sieve.
When cold, remove all membranes and chop the brain with a knife on a cutting board.
Fry the brain well in butter and season with spices.
Pour onto a flat plate, let cool and form into oblong cutlets.
Brush the cutlets with eggs beaten with water and roll in crushed rusks.
Fry nicely golden brown in butter and arrange in a ring on a round plate.
Place peas in the center of the plate.
Serve as a breakfast or light meal dish.

title: Kalvjärpe (Braised Veal Breast)
description: Prepared with veal, lard, and white pepper.
steps: Prepare the meat (see page 232) and cut across into 12 even slices, which are lightly flattened.
Cut the lard into strips, which are dipped in a mixture of salt and pepper, and therewith lard the meat slices.
Roll them up and bind them in two places with fine twine dipped in boiling water.

Brown the butter in an iron pot, place the rolls in and brown them beautifully, sprinkle with the remainder of the spice mixture, dilute with the boiling broth and cream and let them braise slowly with a tight lid until they are tender, or about 3/4 hour.
Remove them, cut off the strings, place them in a warm carrot, whip up the sauce, taste and adjust, and add a little thick cream if needed, and pour over the rolls.
Serve with boiled or pressed potatoes and lingonberries and onion.
If desired, the sauce can be made creamier by thinning it with a little butter and flour.

title: Kalvkarbonad (Veal Chop)
description: Prepared with veal, pork, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 3 hg. fresh pork meat, not too lean
ingredients.sourceText: 3 hg. fresh pork meat, not too lean

steps: Prepare the meat (see p. 232), free from sinews and membranes, cut into pieces and pass 4 times through a meat grinder.

From the forcemeat form cutlets, which are chopped over with a knife so that they get a nice shape, sprinkle with a mixture of salt and white pepper, dip in the beaten eggs and turn in crushed breadcrumbs.
Brown the butter lightly in a frying pan, lay the cutlets in and fry about 3 minutes on each side, after which they are placed in a ring on a warm serving platter.
Whisk out the pan with the water, mixed with meat extract, let the sauce simmer for a couple of minutes, taste and pour over the cutlets.

title: Kalvkotlett i kastrull (Veal Chops in Casserole)
description: Prepared with veal, white pepper, and potatoes.
steps: Dry the chops with a cloth wrung out in hot water, clean them, beat well on both sides and rub with the spice mixture.
Use three small, low, ovenproof forms with lids. Brown the butter in the forms, place one chop in each form and brown nicely.
Peel the potatoes and form them round; lay four pieces around each chop after it is browned.
Sprinkle salt over the potatoes and place the lid on the form.
Put the forms in a hot oven; let the chops and potatoes fry until tender, or about 15 minutes.
Serve in the forms as a breakfast dish.

title: Kalvkotlett à la finesse (Veal Chops with Refinement)
description: Prepared with veal, truffles, and smoked ham.
steps: Cut the truffle, ham and mushrooms into small, even cubes. Chop the trimmings finely and mix with the crushed breadcrumbs.
Dry the chops with a cloth wrung out in hot water, clean them, beat well on both sides and rub with the spice mixture.
Brush with the beaten egg mixed with the water and turn in the ham, mushroom and breadcrumb mixture.
Brown the butter in a frying pan, place the chops in and fry about 5 minutes on each side.
Quickly fry the mushroom and ham cubes in a little of the butter and place in the center of a round serving dish. Place the bread crust around it and lay the chops on top.
Fry the flour well with the butter in which the chops were cooked, add the broth and tomato purée and let the sauce cook 5 minutes.
Taste it and pour over the chops, garnish the dish with French potatoes and parsley and serve as a breakfast dish.

title: Kalvkotletter (Breaded Veal Cutlets)
description: Prepared with veal cutlets, white pepper, and breadcrumbs.
steps: Dry the cutlet rack with a cloth wrung out in hot water.
Cut out the cutlets so that one rib bone remains in each.
Remove the outer membrane and backbone, scrape the meat from the tip of the rib bones and trim them evenly.
Beat the cutlets with a damp meat mallet, shape them and rub in a mixture of salt and pepper.
Heat a frying pan, brown the butter lightly in it, place the cutlets in and fry about 7 minutes on each side, or until they are nicely browned and tender.
Place them on a warm platter and pour the browned butter over them.
If desired, put paper frills on the bones.
Serve with fried potatoes or vegetables. If the cutlets are large, one can suffice for each person and the other ingredients should be reduced accordingly.

description: Prepared with veal cutlets, cream, and white pepper.
steps: Wash the cutlets with a cloth dipped in hot water, trim and pound once on each side.
Sprinkle with pepper and salt, dip in the beaten egg mixed with cream milk and turn in the crushed breadcrumbs.
Brown the cutlets in the heated butter, add the liquid, and let them fry slowly for 10-15 minutes with the lid closed.
Place on a platter, pour the sauce over, and garnish with parsley.
If desired, the breading (egg and crushed breadcrumbs) can be omitted.

Pound the cutlets with a damp meat mallet, shape and rub in with a mixture of salt and pepper.
They can be fried with or without breading. If they are to be breaded, dip them in the beaten eggs and turn them in the crushed rusks.
Heat a frying pan, lightly brown the butter in it, place the cutlets in and fry approximately 7 minutes on each side, or until they are beautifully brown and tender.
Place them on a warm platter and pour the browned butter over them.
If desired, put paper frills on the bones.
Serve with fried potatoes or vegetables. If the cutlets are large, one can be enough for each person and the other ingredients are reduced accordingly.

Add the tomato purée or melted butter with careful stirring.
Serve the veal cutlets in the middle of the platter and the macaroni around them.

title: Kalvkyckling (Veal Birds)
description: Prepared with veal, broth or water, and cream.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water and cut into slices across the grain, pound lightly and sprinkle with pepper and salt.
Rinse, clean and chop the parsley coarsely and work it into 2 tablespoons of the butter.
Divide the parsley butter into as many parts as there are meat slices; place one part on each slice, which is then rolled up and tied with string (previously dipped in boiling water).
Brown the birds in the remaining butter, add boiling broth or water and let them fry on low heat until they feel tender, then remove and take off the strings.
Strain the sauce, skim, finish with cream and serve over the birds.

steps: Rinse the veal liver and cut it into slices.

description: Prepared with veal, lard, and cream.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water, free from membranes and cut straight across the fibers into 2-3 cm thick slices.

title: Kalvrulader (Stuffed Veal Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with veal, white pepper, and meat.

ingredients.name: 200 gr. of the meat for the filling
ingredients.sourceText: 200 gr. of the meat for the filling

ingredients.name: butter (20 gr.) for the filling
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoon butter (20 gr.) for the filling

ingredients.name: salt and white pepper for the filling
ingredients.sourceText: salt and white pepper for the filling

ingredients.name: finely chopped mushrooms or truffle
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoon finely chopped mushrooms or truffle

ingredients.name: 1 1/2 to 2 deciliters thick cream for the filling
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 to 2 deciliters thick cream for the filling

steps: Dry the meat with a cloth wrung out in hot water. Use 200 gr. of it for the filling. Cut the rest into 12 slices, which are beaten well with a damp meat mallet and rubbed in with the spices.
For the meat filling, grind the meat, lard and butter 4 times through a meat grinder.
Pound the filling together with the flour in a stone mortar until it becomes even and smooth, then mix in the spices, onion, mushroom and cream, a little at a time.
Spread the filling on the meat slices, which are then rolled up with the filling inside and tied in two places with fine twine dipped in boiling water.

Brown the butter in an iron pot, place the rolls in and brown them nicely, sprinkle with flour, thin with boiling broth and cream and let them cook with a tightly closed lid until they are tender, or about 3/4 hour.
Remove them, cut off the twine, place in a warm carrot and whisk up the sauce, taste it and pour it over the rolls.
Serve with mashed potatoes or vegetables.

title: Kalvstek (Roast Veal)
description: Prepared with veal, broth or water, and meat stock.
steps: Wash the roast with a cloth dipped in hot water.
Remove the flank and break the spine if the roast is so large that the kidney section is included.
Grease a roasting pan with butter, place the roast in it with the inside up, and put in a hot oven to brown.
When browned, remove it, salt it, and turn it over.
Add the boiling liquid, return the roast to the oven to roast through, and baste with its drippings every ten minutes.
Roasting takes 3-4 hours.
Strain and skim the meat stock, and prepare the sauce according to general sauce rules.

title: Kalvstek i gryta (Braised Veal Roast in Pot)
description: Prepared with veal or chuck, white pepper, and cream.

ingredients.name: veal chuck or similar cut
ingredients.sourceText: 2 kg veal chuck or similar cut

steps: The meat, which should have hung so that it is tender, is pounded on the skin side with a damp mallet, dried with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and rubbed with the spices.
The butter is browned in a cooking pot, which should not be larger than to just fit the meat.

The roast is placed in and browned well on all sides, after which the lid is placed on and the roast is allowed to cook slowly without adding liquid, until it is tender, or about 3 hours. It is turned often and the lid should fit tightly on the pot.
The roast is placed with the inner side up on a warm platter and carved at the table.
Most of the fat is skimmed from the gravy in the pot, after which the flour is mixed well with the meat gravy, the cream is added and the sauce is allowed to boil for 8 minutes.
It is seasoned with the spices and poured through a sauce strainer into a warm sauce bowl.
The roast is served with vegetables or potatoes and cucumber as well as salads.

title: Kalvsylta (Calf Aspic)
description: Prepared with meat, peppercorns, and white pepper.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water and place it in boiling water.
When the broth comes to a boil, skim it well and add the peppercorns and 1.5 tablespoons salt.
Let it simmer slowly until the meat is tender.
Remove the meat, let it cool and then chop it fairly finely.
Let the broth reduce during this time.
Add the meat and bring everything to a boil.
Season strongly with salt, pepper and ginger.

title: Kalvtimbal (Veal Timbal)
description: Prepared with veal, cream, and white pepper.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water, free it from sinews and membranes, cut into cubes and pass three times through a meat grinder.
Pound it in a stone mortar together with the butter and egg yolks.
Work the cream together with flour, salt and white pepper into the forcemeat.
Butter a fine metal mold and garnish it with blanched macaroni, cut into rings and stars.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff and fold them last into the forcemeat, which is immediately poured into the prepared mold.
Bind the mold over with butter paper and poach the timbal in a water bath in an oven or on the stove for 1-1.5 hours.
Turn it out and serve with preserved peas, poured over with clarified butter.

title: Kalvtunga med Maderasås (Calf Tongue with Madeira Sauce)
description: A sauce made with tongue, madeira, and white pepper.
steps: Brush the tongue well, rinse it, place it in the boiling water with salt added, and let it boil until the skin can be easily pulled off.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, place the tongue in and brown it nicely on all sides, salt it and dilute with the broth, with soy sauce added.
Let it cook slowly until it is tender, approximately 1 hour, and baste it every ten minutes so it does not dry out.
Slice it, arrange it on a warm serving dish and garnish with small bread croutons.
Thicken the meat stock with the mondamin flour, stirred in the wine, and let the sauce boil approximately 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and season the sauce with salt and pepper.
Pour a little of the sauce over the tongue and pour the rest into a sauce boat.
Serve as a breakfast dish with browned potatoes.

title: Kalvtungor med Kapris (Calf Tongues with Capers)
description: Prepared with tongues, capers, and carrot.

ingredients.name: crushed bread crumbs for breading
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons crushed bread crumbs for breading

steps: Let the tongues soak in cold water for 1 hour.
Scald them and scrape well.
Place them in boiling water and skim thoroughly when the broth comes to a boil.
Add salt and root vegetables, and let the tongues cook slowly until tender.
When done, remove the skin immediately and cut the meat into fine cubes.
Combine butter and flour, add the cooking broth, place the tongue and finely chopped capers in, and let the stew cook for 10 minutes, then taste for seasoning.
Spread the mixture on a flat dish to cool, and form small sugar-loaf shaped croquettes.
Roll in crushed bread crumbs, dip in whisked egg, and roll again in crushed bread crumbs.
Let stand to dry for ½ hour.
Heat the lard, cook the croquettes golden-brown in it, and place on brown paper to drain.
Garnish with parsley and serve with mushroom or brown sauce.

title: Kanapéer (Canapés)
description: Prepared with wheat flour, ice, and butter.
steps: Prepare the butter dough as fine butter dough (no. 548)
Roll out the dough into an oblong cake of 1 cm thickness
Sprinkle sugar over it and fold the bottom dough in three parts
Tap it out slightly lengthwise and fold it across the middle (from left to right), sprinkle with sugar and roll out again to a cake of 2 cm thickness and 15 cm width
Fold the dough double along the middle, from top to bottom
Tap the dough at the top edge and cut into 1 cm thick slices
Turn these in sugar and place on a well-dried baking sheet with the cut side down in rows with 10 cm between the rows

title: Kanapéer (Sugar-Layered Pastries)

Roll it out into an oblong rectangle of 1/2 cm. thickness and sprinkle with sugar, then fold as with regular butter dough, but sprinkle sugar between each fold.
Fold 3 times in the same manner and sprinkle with sugar.

With a sharp knife, cut across the dough approximately 1/2 cm. wide strips, which are placed cut-side down on a well-cleaned baking sheet.
Bake immediately in a warm oven and turn once during baking so they become nicely golden-brown on both sides.
When cooled, place two together with jam between.

title: Kandering av mandelmassa och nötter (Candied Almond Paste and Nuts)
description: Prepared with sweet almonds, powdered sugar, and walnuts.
steps: Prepare almond paste from sweet almonds, powdered sugar, and water. Divide into four equal parts.
Color one part bright red with carmine, one part light green with caramel coloring, one part brown with cocoa powder, and leave the last quarter white.
Gently crack walnuts, remove shells, and join walnut halves together with the uncolored almond paste. Roll the remaining almond paste into small balls.
Cook rock sugar, water, and glucose to caramel or strong crack stage (see sugar cooking). Cool rapidly by dipping the pan briefly in cold water.
Drop walnuts and almond paste balls one at a time into the sugar, lift out with two small silver forks dipped in food oil, and place on oiled marble or stone slab.
Similarly candy peeled brazil nuts (with inner brown skin scraped off, coloring the sugar layer red with carmine), peeled Spanish nuts, orange segments, grapes, etc.

title: Kanin med Curry och Ris (Rabbit with Curry and Rice)
description: Prepared with rabbit, onion, and curry powder.
steps: The rabbit is treated and cut as in the previous recipe.
The butter is browned in an iron pot, the meat is added, browned nicely and removed with a slotted spoon.
The onion, flour and curry powder are added and fried well with the butter in the pot, the broth is diluted, and the sauce is brought to a boil.
The meat is placed in the sauce, the lemon juice is added and the meat is allowed to simmer slowly with a tightly closed lid until it is tender, or about 1 hour.
Place it on a warm plate, whisk up the sauce with the cream, bring it to a boil, taste it and pour it over the meat.
Around the meat garnish with boiled rice, sprinkled with 1-2 teaspoons curry powder.

title: Karolina Rice Pudding (Swedish Rice and Orange Pudding)
description: A pudding made with rice, oranges, and cream.
steps: Rinse the rice grains, scald them in hot water, place in boiling water and let them cook until soft, about 20 minutes.
Strain the rice and rinse with cold water, letting it drain well.
Peel the oranges, remove the white pith carefully, then cut them into small cubes, remove the pits and mix with the sugar.
Whip the cream until stiff peaks form.
Rinse the gelatin with cold water, cut into pieces and dissolve in 3 tbsp. hot water.
Mix the rice grains with the orange cubes and cream, and lastly add the gelatin.
Pour the mixture into a water-rinsed mold dusted with sugar and let it stand on ice about 3 hours, or until set.
Loosen the pudding around the edge with a pointed knife, unmold onto a flat glass dish with parchment paper, garnish with orange wedges and serve with orange sauce.

title: Kastanjepuré (Chestnut Puree)

Press through a sieve.
Mix the puree with butter and cream, heat it, and season with the spices.
Serve preferably in pastry shells.

title: Katrinplommonkaka (Prune Cake)
description: A cake made with prunes, cream, and sugar.

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr) for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp butter (10 gr) for the pan

steps: The prunes are rinsed well in several lukewarm waters and placed in a stoneware pot in alternating layers with the sugar.
Water is added and the prunes are left to soak overnight.
They are then boiled for approximately 5 minutes, left to cool, pitted, cut into strips, which are placed in a greased pie pan.
The pits are crushed, the almonds are placed in boiling water, peeled, dried in the oven, chopped finely and sprinkled over the prunes.

Egg yolks, sugar and butter are stirred for 20 minutes, the boiling cream is added with strong whisking together with the lemon zest, and the whisking is continued until the cream is cold, then the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks are folded in carefully.
The cream is poured over the prunes.

steps: Rinse the prunes very thoroughly in several portions of lukewarm water and let them soak in cold water overnight.

Serve cold with whipped cream.

title: Katrinplommonkräm (Prune Cream)
description: Prepared with prunes, wine, and potato flour.
steps: Rinse the prunes very well and layer alternately with the sugar in a bowl, add water, and let the prunes stand overnight.
Cut them in half lengthwise and remove the pits.
Crush half of the pits, scald the almonds and chop finely.
Put the prunes together with the almonds in the water they were soaked in, add the wine, and let the prunes boil until they are properly soft.
Thicken the cream with the potato flour mixed in 1/2 dcl cold water, let boil for 2 minutes, taste and pour into a compote bowl rinsed with warm water.
Serve cold with cream or milk.

ingredients.name: 30 gr. melted butter for the molds
ingredients.sourceText: 30 gr. melted butter for the molds

ingredients.name: 1/2 batch vanilla cream (recipe no. 871) or 1/2 batch lemon cream (recipe no. 869)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 batch vanilla cream (recipe no. 871) or 1/2 batch lemon cream (recipe no. 869)

steps: Grease small fluted pastry molds with melted butter and allow to set, then dust with sifted bread crumbs.
Whip three whole eggs and three egg yolks for 45 minutes, then add the finely grated lemon zest or 15 gr. blanched and ground sweet almond and the flour.
Last, fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Fill the molds three-quarters full with batter and bake in a not-too-hot oven.
Turn out the pastries and allow to cool, split them open, and fill with cream.
Glaze (recipe no. 961), dust with finely chopped orange peels and pistachios, and serve as dessert or with coffee and tea.

title: Kejsarbakelser (Emperor Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolk, almond, and bitter almonds.
steps: Prepare the pastry dough as simple pastry dough (recipe no. 974) and let it rest in a cool place for about 2 hours.
Blanch the almonds, dry them, grind them through a mill, and pound with the sugar and egg whites in a mortar until a fine and smooth paste.
Prepare the cream as in recipe no. 871 and it should be quite firm.
Roll out the pastry dough to 3 mm thickness and cut out into oval cakes with a mold, place on a buttered sheet, and bake until nicely golden brown in a not-too-hot oven.
When cooled, place 1 tsp. cream on each cake and top with a layer of almond paste.
(The almond paste is pressed into oblong, fluted molds and turned over the cream.)
Glaze the almond paste (recipe no. 961), dust with blanched and finely chopped pistachios, then let the pastries stand a few minutes in gentle oven heat to dry.

title: Kejsarsoppa (Emperor's Soup)
description: A soup made with broth, sherry or madeira, and egg yolks.
steps: Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the boiling broth and let it cook while stirring for 5 minutes, then season with spices and wine.
Whisk the egg yolks in the soup bowl and pour the soup over them while whisking vigorously. Serve very hot with egg balls.

title: Klappgröt (Whipped Grain Porridge)
description: Prepared with fruit juice, semolina, and potato flour.
steps: Boil the water and fruit juice together, whisk in the semolina and let it cook about 10 minutes
Finish the porridge with the potato flour dissolved in a little cold water and bring to a good boil
Pour immediately into a stone pot placed in cold water
Whip the porridge vigorously with a steel whisk for 20 minutes, or until it is light red and fluffy
Serve with good milk

title: Klar Buljong (Clear Beef Broth)
description: A soup made with beef, carrot, and parsnip.
steps: The broth should preferably be cooked the day before it is to be used.
Prepare the meat and cook the broth as in the preceding recipe.
If desired, add the peeled red onion with a clove inserted into it at the same time as the vegetables.

The meat used for clarification should be dried with a cloth, wrung out in cold water, cut into small dice and pounded together with the egg white and rinsed eggshell in a stone mortar with a wooden pestle until a fine mass is obtained, which is placed in a soup pot with a thick bottom.
Carefully remove the fat cake from the broth, then pour it into the pot, but the sediment at the bottom must not come along.
Place the pot over the fire and let the broth come to a boil and boil for 5 minutes with frequent stirring at the bottom.
Then set the pot to the side of the stove, cover it and let the broth stand for 1 hour without boiling, but keep it hot.
Strain it through a flannel sieve wrung out in hot water and measure it.
It can be brought to a boil; if it is more than 1 1/2 liters, the broth can be boiled down until the desired amount is obtained.

Season the broth with salt and cayenne and serve with various kinds of garnish, such as strips of tongue, truffle and mushrooms, asparagus tips, vegetables, egg royal, quenelles of fish, veal or chicken forcemeat, cheese fritters, cheese sticks, pastries, croutons, vermicelli, dumplings, etc.
If the broth is to be used for reduced soups or purées, 2 liters of water can be taken per 1 kg of meat; the broth should then not be boiled down.

title: Klar Buljong (Clear Broth)
description: A soup made with marrow or beef, carrots, and parsnip.

ingredients.name: marrow bone, beef neck or rib
ingredients.sourceText: 2 kg marrow bone, beef neck or rib

ingredients.name: a few sprigs of parsley (for clarification)
ingredients.sourceText: a few sprigs of parsley (for clarification)

steps: The meat, preferably freshly slaughtered, is washed with a cloth dipped in cold water, cut into small pieces, and placed in cold water in a tall pot of copper or enameled iron with a tight-fitting lid.
Salt is added at once, after which the kettle is left at the side of the fire for 1/2 hour.
The whole is then brought slowly to a boil, skimmed very well when it comes to a boil, and is then allowed to simmer slowly for 5-6 hours.

During the first hour the broth is boiling, all the scum that floats to the surface is carefully skimmed. (One can add a little cold water, so that the boiling stops for a moment, and when the broth boils again, it is skimmed at once.)
After the broth has been boiling for a couple of hours, the roasted and rinsed vegetables are added along with the peppercorns.
When the broth has cooked its full time, it is strained and left to stand until the fat has risen to the top, after which this is very well skimmed off.
It is best if the broth is cooked the day before it will be used.
For clarification, the ground meat is mixed with the egg whites and the chopped vegetables, and the cold broth is stirred into this little by little.
The broth is then allowed to boil for 15 minutes and is then strained through a cloth or woolen cloth wrung out in hot water.
Broth can also be clarified with whole eggs. It will have a beautiful color from the yolk and will be clear.
If the broth is cooked the day before it will be used, clarifying agents may be unnecessary.
If brown broth is desired, the meat is browned before cooking.

title: Klar buljong med grönsaker (Clear Broth with Vegetables)
description: A soup made with broth, carrot, and parsnip.
steps: Scrape, rinse, and dry the roots, then cut into fine dice
Cut the leek into fine strips
Trim and shape the Jerusalem artichokes into rounds
Clean the cauliflower and divide into smaller pieces
Place the vegetables in boiling water with salt and sugar and let cook for 5 minutes
Add the cauliflower and let everything cook until tender
Bring the broth to a boil and add the cooked vegetables along with ¼ liter of the cooking liquid
Season the soup with salt and cayenne and serve very hot

title: Klar Äppelsoppa (Clear Apple Soup)
description: A soup made with apples, lemon, and wine or sherry.
steps: Rinse and dry the apples. Do not peel 1 liter of them; cut them into wedges and remove the flower, stem, and core.
Put them in cold water and let them cook until soft but not falling apart or mushing.
Pour them into cheesecloth and let the liquid drain. (The pulp can be cooked again and the liquid used for cream.)
Peel the remaining apples, cut them into 6 wedges, and cook them with the lemon zest, sugar, and wine in the apple liquid until soft.
Thicken the soup with the potato flour mixed in 1/2 coffee spoon cold water and let it cook 2 minutes.
Taste it, let it cool, and add small dollops of currant jelly.
Serve with rusks or biscuits.

title: Klenäter (Fried Pastry Knots)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolks, egg white, and powdered sugar.
steps: Stir the eggs and sugar for 1 hour in the same direction.
Thereafter add the cream beaten to stiff peaks, the cognac, and lastly the flour.
Work the dough very well so that it becomes tough.
Cover it and let it rest overnight, otherwise it is very difficult to roll out.

Roll out the dough to 2 mm. thickness and cut with a pastry cutter into squares, which are folded at the corners, strips which are twisted, or into oblong cakes, on whose middle a slit is made, and thereby one end of the cake is drawn through so that a knot is formed in the middle.
Heat the lard together with 1 tbsp. brandy, whereupon a raw potato slice is placed in it (when the potato slice becomes dark brown, a new one is placed).
Place the pastries—not too many at once—and cook until light yellow, lay them on gray paper to drain and fan them with a wing or with a bellows, if you have one.

title: Klimp (Almond Dumplings)
description: Prepared with bitter almonds, sweet almonds, and butter.
steps: Mix butter and flour together, gradually add the milk a little at a time, and let the mixture cook for 15 minutes
Remove the pot from the side of the fire; add the blanched and grated bitter almond, sugar, and beaten eggs
Let the klimp simmer over the fire until it becomes thick
Cool it in a water-rinsed mold and turn it out once cooled
If serving with fruit soup, garnish with blanched sweet almonds cut into strips
If using with broth, garnish with chopped parsley
